review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner; self-review, not independent approval
review.decision: Carry connection cancellation through actual heartbeat, compatibility rebind and recovery writes
review.notes: Follow up independent exact Re1a44 heartbeat P1. Previously fixed activation publication serialization, Run shutdown, zero-attempt cancellation and strict owner guards remain unchanged. Add context-aware Refresh while preserving its public background-context compatibility wrapper. The actual production binding factory must supply its own lifetime context to heartbeat, not only to ordinary Bind. All Refresh branches, especially same-thread legacy hook with empty Frontend, propagate that context into actual Bind; a cancellation during strict proof must prevent not-yet-started writes. Check context around direct recovery/checkpoint/receipt writes too. Already-started atomic IO is not forcibly undone; retire only the exact live receipt this call wrote, preserve committed history/replacement owners, keep lease ordering and avoid recursive binding lease. Committed regressions exercise real factory callback context and real resume fixture legacy rebind/recovery/normal refresh publication. Also re-run the retained independent actual factory→tick→permit→Refresh→Bind integration fixture in a new task-only source snapshot with exact old-R/new-candidate maps; its synthetic proof adapters are fixture-only, never shipped or confused with real sessions. Test controls must fail target assertions, not compilation. Do not claim post-return discard/close cleanup proves no publication. No real binding, session, restore, input, queue or service operations.

cases.description: Heartbeat publication uses the live connection context at actual writes and compatibility Bind
cases.setup: Actual production binding factory callback and isolated real resume frontend fixture; deterministic strict-observation/write seams; retained independent integration adapter source
cases.action: Cancel in same-thread old-hook rebind strict proof; cancel while recovering a missing index or checkpoint/receipt write; replace live receipt during partial cleanup; call the actual factory heartbeat after its parent is canceled
cases.expected: Canceled proof causes zero not-yet-started receipt/index writes and no new live authority before close. Factory callback returns the actual cancellation cause. Partial IO only retires its own exact written live proof, retains committed history and a replacement owner. Valid uncanceled legacy/missing-index recovery and original guards remain; no recursive lease or new lock cycle.
